name: Julie Byrne
label: Ghostly International
lede: She learned guitar at seventeen on her father's instrument, worked as a Central Park ranger, then took six years to follow a cult-favorite record, and the wait ended with Pitchfork's Best New Music and a No. 21 finish on its 2023 list.

eras.title: A guitar that was her father's
eras.text: Born in Buffalo, Byrne took up her father's instrument as a teenager, left home at eighteen and spent years drifting through half a dozen cities. Her first songs went out on cassette.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne · Wikipedia: The Greater Wings
years.p: Her father played fingerstyle guitar. When multiple sclerosis complications meant he no longer could, Byrne picked up the instrument herself at seventeen.
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Byrne has described learning his guitar as "an offering to him", a chance to honor the craft he could no longer practice.

Her later records keep that fingerstyle core, even as the third one adds synthesizer, harp and strings.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne · Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne
years.h: Byrne leaves Buffalo and keeps moving
years.p: Wikipedia lists Pittsburgh, Northampton, Chicago, Lawrence, Seattle and New Orleans before she lands in New York.
years.xp: Stereogum quotes her on the other side of that restlessness, years later: "I'm not willing to live the way that I did before." By then she was trying to stay put.

eras.title: Rooms, rangers and Not Even Happiness
eras.text: Two cassettes became a debut, a job in Central Park became a second life, and a record made in her childhood home made her name in indie circles.

years.src: Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne · Wikipedia: Julie Byrne
years.h: Rooms with Walls and Windows collects two cassettes
years.p: The debut compiles two cassette-only releases from 2012 and 2013, her self-titled tape and You Would Love It Here.
years.xp: Stereogum's Q&A says the tapes were recorded live in Chicago in a show space.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne · Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne
years.h: Byrne works as a seasonal ranger in Central Park
years.p: She had studied environmental science, and Wikipedia quotes her calling the park a sanctuary for New Yorkers and for wildlife.
years.xp: Stereogum reports the job answered her need for green space while living in New York City.

years.src: Wikipedia: Not Even Happiness · Stereogum: Q&A: Julie Byrne
years.h: Not Even Happiness lands: nine songs, 32 minutes, Buffalo
years.p: Basin Rock released it in the UK on January 13 and Ba Da Bing in the US on January 27. Pitchfork gave it 8.3.
years.xp:
Eric Littmann produced, recorded and mixed it in Buffalo, and Stereogum places the sessions at Byrne's childhood home. Jake Falby's string arrangements were done at a cabin in Holderness, New Hampshire. Michele Finkelstein played flute, Chris Masullo guitar and Johanna Warren sang backing vocals.

Wikipedia lists a Metacritic score of 82 from 22 critics, and year-end spots at Spin (No. 9), Stereogum (No. 20) and Paste (No. 27).

years.h: "Natural Blue" comes out of a 40-day tour
years.p: Byrne wrote the song after an emotionally heavy night in Boulder, before a 10-hour drive to Kansas, she told Stereogum.
years.xp: She described a tour with almost no rest. It is the touring life written down in real time.

eras.title: Six years, one loss
eras.text: The follow-up was started with Eric Littmann in Chicago, interrupted by a pandemic and by his death, and finished with a new producer.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Greater Wings · Loud and Quiet: Julie Byrne · 13th Floor: Julie Byrne Remains On The Edge Of Mystery
years.h: Sessions for The Greater Wings begin with Eric Littmann
years.p: Wikipedia dates the first recording to 2018 in Chicago, where Littmann kept a home studio.
years.xp:
Other interviews put the restart at 2019 or early 2020, so the start date is loose. Byrne told Loud and Quiet she began writing the first chords in 2017, right after Not Even Happiness.

She said of the long gap: "The songs in and of themselves are stories that needed to be lived out and that took time."

years.cap: Julie Byrne at Sea Change, Totnes · Wikimedia
years.src: Wikipedia: The Greater Wings · Paste: How Julie Byrne Found New Heights
years.h: Eric Littmann, her collaborator and partner, dies unexpectedly
years.p: Wikipedia says Littmann was Byrne's partner and was producing The Greater Wings when he died in 2021. The sessions stopped.
years.xp:
Byrne has said of the collaboration: "It wasn't even his vision or technical skill or artistry that made the collaboration so rich and singular, it was his love and care."

Paste describes him as a University of Chicago lab manager who co-produced with a portable suitcase recording setup. Sources do not state a cause of death.

years.src: 13th Floor: Julie Byrne Remains On The Edge Of Mystery · Paste: How Julie Byrne Found New Heights · Wikipedia: The Greater Wings
years.h: Alex Somers takes over production in the Catskills
years.p: Alex Somers helps Byrne finish the record with collaborators she already had.
years.xp:
13th Floor reports production resumed in early 2022 in the Catskills. Jake Falby, who arranged strings on Not Even Happiness, returned for violin, guitar, piano and synth sessions in Los Angeles, according to Paste.

Byrne on Somers: "Being a producer is such an art... it's also a grace of relationship."

eras.title: The Greater Wings
eras.text: After six years, three singles and a record about grief, Byrne was suddenly everywhere on critics' lists.

years.h: "Summer Glass" is the first new music in six years
years.p: The lead single announces The Greater Wings on Ghostly International.

years.src: Paste: Listen to Julie Byrne's New Single Moonless · 13th Floor: Julie Byrne Remains On The Edge Of Mystery
years.h: "Moonless": her first song written on piano
years.p: Byrne wrote it during an artist residency in Culatra, Portugal, and calls it a breakup song.
years.xp:
Paste says she wrote it walking the dunes on the ocean side of Culatra, with dock noises, tidal-flat smells and a coast in constant erosion on her mind.

13th Floor adds that she began piano lessons at 28.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Greater Wings · Metacritic: The Greater Wings · Pitchfork on X: Julie Byrne's The Greater Wings is named Best New Music
years.h: The Greater Wings: Pitchfork gives it 8.5 and Best New Music
years.p: Ghostly released the ten-song album on July 7. Pitchfork gave it 8.5, per Wikipedia's reception table, and Metacritic lists 91 from 13 critics.
years.xp:
The album was recorded across 2018, 2021 and 2022 in Chicago, Buffalo and Los Angeles, with Jake Falby, Eric Littmann and Alex Somers credited as producers. It adds synthesizer, harp and strings to her guitar.

The Guardian gave it 5/5 and AllMusic 4.5/5. Wikipedia reports it as her first US chart appearance, at No. 90 on Top Current Album Sales.

years.src: Wikipedia: Julie Byrne with Laugh Cry Laugh
years.h: Julie Byrne with Laugh Cry Laugh EP
years.p: Four tracks, 11 minutes, on Ghostly, including a cover of a Jackson Browne song.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Emily Fontana on bass and Taryn Blake Miller on recording and engineering. Paste ranked it the 24th best EP of 2023.

years.h: Pitchfork ranks The Greater Wings No. 21 of 2023
years.p: It also lands at No. 6 at Paste, No. 10 at Mojo and No. 9 at Uncut.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the album was nominated for Best Folk Record at the 2024 Libera Awards.
